title: Swapping letters
syllabusUnit: Unit I: Classical Ciphers & Substitution Techniques
learningGoals: You will be able to encrypt and decrypt messages with the Caesar shift.
You will be able to construct a 5x5 Playfair cipher matrix.
You will be able to use a keyword table in the Vigenère polyalphabetic cipher.

lessonCards.title: Caesar & Monoalphabetic Ciphers
lessonCards.analogy: Rotating an alphabet decoder ring so A turns into D and B turns into E.
lessonCards.coreConcept: Caesar shifts every letter by a fixed key k: C = (P + k) mod 26. Monoalphabetic replaces each character with a fixed substitute.

lessonCards.title: The Playfair 5x5 Grid
lessonCards.analogy: Pairing letters like dance partners and swapping them using a square coordinate grid.
lessonCards.coreConcept: Playfair encrypts pairs of letters (digraphs) using a 5x5 matrix filled with a keyword (merging I and J into one cell).
lessonCards.example: Letters in the same row shift right; letters in the same column shift down; rectangles swap corners.

lessonCards.title: Vigenère: Polyalphabetic Armor
lessonCards.analogy: Using a secret password where each letter provides a different Caesar shift dial.
lessonCards.coreConcept: Vigenère uses a repeating keyword. Each keyword letter selects a different Caesar shift, flattening single-letter frequency peaks.
lessonCards.example: Key 'KEY' shifts letter 1 by 10, letter 2 by 4, and letter 3 by 24 repeatedly.

questions.prompt: Using a Caesar cipher with key k = 3, what is the encryption of the word 'SECURITY'?
options: VHFXULWB
TFDUJUZ
WIGYVMX
RDDFSJSX
questions.explanation: S->V, E->H, C->F, U->X, R->U, I->L, T->W, Y->B (wrapping around Z).
wrongExplanations: Correct! Every letter shifted forward by 3 modulo 26.
This option applied key = 1.
This option applied key = 4.
This option shifted backwards by 1.
questions.realWorldExample: Julius Caesar historically used key = 3 to protect military orders sent to his generals in Gaul.

questions.prompt: How does the Playfair cipher handle duplicate letters within the same digraph pair (e.g. 'LL' in 'BALLOON')?
options: It inserts an uncommon filler letter like 'X' between them
It ignores the duplicate letter completely
It deletes the entire word
It converts both letters into digits 00
questions.explanation: Playfair rules require inserting a dummy filler letter (usually 'X' or 'Q') between identical letters in a pair.
wrongExplanations: Correct! 'LL' becomes 'LX' and 'LO' to ensure distinct matrix lookups.
Ignoring duplicates destroys clean decryption.
Playfair never deletes words.
Classical Playfair operates on a 5x5 alphabet grid.
questions.realWorldExample: The British military used Playfair in the Boer War and WWI because it required no mechanical machinery.

questions.prompt: Why is the Vigenère cipher called 'polyalphabetic'?
options: It uses multiple shift alphabets determined by the repeating keyword
It requires 26 computers running in parallel
It translates text into multiple spoken languages
It only operates on polygons
questions.explanation: Because each character in the repeating key defines a different Caesar alphabet shift for successive characters.
wrongExplanations: Correct! Polyalphabetic means many alphabets are applied in rotation.
Classical Vigenère was calculated by hand using a tableau.
It operates on single-language character sets.
Geometry has nothing to do with it.
questions.realWorldExample: Vigenère was hailed as 'le chiffre indéchiffrable' for over two centuries.

questions.prompt: In a 5x5 Playfair grid, how many total letters can fit, and how is the 26-letter English alphabet accommodated?
options: 25 letters fit; I and J share a single combined cell
24 letters fit; vowels are removed
30 letters fit; punctuation marks are added
26 letters fit; the grid uses non-square cells
questions.explanation: 5x5 = 25 cells. The letters I and J are merged into one cell to fit the 26-letter Latin alphabet.
wrongExplanations: Correct! Standard Playfair merges 'I' and 'J' in the same square.
Vowels are essential to decryption.
A 5x5 grid contains 25 positions.
A grid with 26 cells cannot be a 5x5 square.
questions.realWorldExample: John F. Kennedy's PT-109 rescue message was encoded with a Playfair cipher variant in WWII.

questions.prompt: Which classical cipher uses linear algebra and matrix multiplication (C = K * P mod 26) to encrypt blocks of letters?
options: Hill Cipher
Caesar Cipher
Rail Fence Cipher
Atbash Cipher
questions.explanation: Lester Hill invented the Hill cipher in 1929, using matrix multiplication modulo 26 to encrypt polygraphic blocks.
wrongExplanations: Correct! Hill cipher encrypts m letters simultaneously using an m x m matrix key.
Caesar cipher uses simple single-letter addition.
Rail fence is a transposition cipher.
Atbash is a Hebrew reversal cipher.
questions.realWorldExample: Hill cipher was the first polygraphic cipher practical to operate on more than 3 symbols at once.

questions.prompt: What is the primary weakness of all simple monoalphabetic substitution ciphers?
options: They preserve the natural letter frequency distribution of the language
They require keys longer than the internet
They produce ciphertexts twice as long as the plaintext
They can only be decrypted at night
questions.explanation: If 'E' is the most frequent letter in English, its substitute will also appear most frequently in the ciphertext.
wrongExplanations: Correct! Frequency analysis quickly breaks monoalphabetic ciphers by counting symbol occurrences.
Monoalphabetic keys are only 26 characters long.
Substitution replaces 1 letter with 1 letter.
Time of day has no influence on cryptographic mathematics.
questions.realWorldExample: Arab mathematician Al-Kindi discovered frequency cryptanalysis in the 9th century to break substitution ciphers.

ashRecap: Substitution swaps letters for other letters. Vigenère uses a keyword to make letter frequencies much harder to trace!
